title: Choose the visual world for the Bloop parent page
question: One page, an age dial from 6 to 17, the whole theme grows up as it turns. The roll assigned Channel Bloop. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Channel Bloop
options.lineage: Kids' TV channel idents that grow into a teen documentary channel
options.thesis: The age dial is a channel dial: every age is its own channel with its own ident, schedule and host.
options.viewport: A channel ident hero (bouncy Bloop at 6, a documentary title card at 17) with the week's lessons below as the programme guide and Book a free lesson on the guide.
options.risk: Frames lessons as TV to parents worried about screen time, while 6-8 lessons are mostly unplugged.

raised.raise: One cord: every color, radius and type weight interpolates from the dial, nothing swaps abruptly.
Ornament density follows age: shapes crowd in at 6 and recede to one rule at 17.
The age numeral is the hero object, a big physical digit that turns with the dial.

options.label: The Exercise Book
options.lineage: School stationery from crayon scrapbook to dot-grid planner
options.thesis: The page is your child's notebook: the ruling, the pen and the handwriting grow up as the dial turns.
materials: real notebook rulings: blank, wide, squared, dot grid
options.viewport: An open exercise book: crayon and stickers at 6, squared paper and ballpoint at 13, a dot-grid planner at 16; lesson proof (Made, How, Think) pasted in as the child's own work, Book a free lesson in the margin.
options.risk: The notebook is a familiar education metaphor; rulings must structure real content, not decorate.

options.label: Deeper Every Year
options.lineage: A dive from turquoise surface to deep water
options.thesis: Age is depth: bright surface at 6, deep ink at 17. Same habits, deeper each year.
materials: water light that dims by depth
options.viewport: A vertical depth gauge that reads the child's age; Bloop sinks as the dial moves; lessons sit at their depth.
options.case: Fuses cleanly with 'deeper each year'; loses on audience: parents do not see their child in a diver.
options.risk: The deep end can feel cold or scary to parents who want ambition for their teen.

options.label: Toy Catalogue Spread
options.lineage: Eighties toy catalogues in unmixed primaries
options.thesis: Courses packed like the catalogue parents grew up with, each with a burst flash.
options.viewport: An edge-to-edge spread of the age's courses, a burst flash shouting First lesson free.
options.case: Parents feel the nostalgia and the offer is clear; loses at 15-17 where a toy catalogue reads childish.
options.risk: Cannot get serious enough for teens without abandoning the world.

options.label: Drawcord Cape
options.lineage: A flat cape that one pulled cord shapes into volume
options.thesis: One pull transforms a flat plane into structure.
options.viewport: A black semicircle that gathers as the cord is pulled.
options.case: Right mechanism, wrong world: black silk and gold cannot be childish at 6.
options.kept: One control drives the whole transformation.
options.risk: Luxury fashion has nothing to say to a parent of a 7-year-old.

options.label: Nixie Counter
options.case: Too technical and cold at the young end.
options.kept: The age number as a physical, turning digit.
options.risk: Reads as a lab instrument, not a school.

options.label: Algorave Floor
options.thesis: Edits apply on the next beat, visible before they sound.
options.viewport: A code buffer as the stage.
options.case: Parents of 6-year-olds do not identify with a club.
options.kept: Show what will change before it changes.
options.risk: Alienates every parent below the 15-17 end.

options.label: Secession Page
options.thesis: Ornament grows in from the margins toward the text.
options.viewport: A clearing of text inside a growing border.
options.case: Beautiful, but no link to AI, kids or parents.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A kids edtech landing page, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Headline and mascot split hero, age tabs, course cards, pricing, FAQ.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every kids coding school ad parents already scroll past.
